speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can breath and kin be the knower?
premises: Though joined (samavāyin) with knowing and the rest, breath-and-kin are never proved (na siddhaḥ) by non-spreading (aprathana).
They would be knowables (prameyam), never knower (pramātā) — otherwise, delusion (anyato bhramāt).
Vṛ: the measured knower, joined with knowing-qualities, still fails by grasp-lack; grasp-lessness means inertia-compatriot; the breath-cage's knowability is borrowed error.
inference: Breath is demoted to knowable: the knower cannot be what never spreads.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Does the confined order escape the self?
premises: Though thing-abiding stands locked in the living (jīve niruddhā), curbed by breath and the eightfold city (prāṇapuryaṣṭakaniyantrite).
Even there, it abides (sthitā) in the supreme self (paramātmani).

Vṛ: in transactional living, all outer-inner order is curbed in contracted living — yet by contraction-lifting, as one with the higher knower, it stands in Śiva-self alone, since breath is non-separate from awareness-shine.
inference: Confinement is rehoused: even locked order abides in the supreme self.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can breath restrain that self-nature?
premises: How (katham) could restraint (yantraṇā) by breath of him, of that self (tadātmana), ever be proved (sādhitā) — in recognition (pratyabhijñāyām)?
By living-ness (jīvatā), beyond non-showing (akhyāteḥ param).

Vṛ: how could breath-knowers veil unbroken full-I-flashing Śiva? Bondage is just unspreading of boundless power — called living-ness — settled at length in the Īśvarapratyabhijñā; discriminate thence.
inference: Breath-restraint is unprovable; living-ness outlies non-showing — recognition, not breath, settles it.
uncertainties: sādhitā's scope parsed with the Vṛ: restraint unprovable (kathaṃ), living-ness beyond non-showing — the nominal close read as verdict, not afterthought.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Where lies the ordering of things?
premises: No thing-ordering (nārthavyavasthā) lies in breath-and-kin through I-blocking (ahaṃbhāvanirodhataḥ).
Shining's self-rest (prakāśasyātmaviśrāntiḥ) is sung (kīrtitaḥ) as I-ness (ahaṃbhāvaḥ) — indeed (hi).
Vṛ: blocking the grasp (parāmarśa) that is mere self-shining, no thing-order holds, since order rests in awareness; self-rest of awareness is full-I-grasp by nature — the thing-orderer is sung.
inference: Order is not in breath but in I-ness: shining's self-rest, sung as the orderer.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What unfolds from rest?
premises: Told already (uktā): that rest (sā eva viśrāntiḥ — feminine, resumed) by blocking of all dependence (sarvāpekṣānirodhataḥ).
Freedom (svātantryam), then doership (kartṛtvaṃ) foremost (mukhyam), and lordship (īśvaratā) with it.
Vṛ: that same rest — end-ground of world-things' final standing — is freedom (needing no kit beyond itself), foremost doership, and the lordship the āgamas trumpet.
inference: Rest unfolds: freedom, then doership, then lordship — the absolute's offices from dependence-blocked rest.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Whence Māyā and world-making?
premises: Called Māyā (māyābhidāḥ), of his power alone (tacchakter eva — tat+śakteḥ, Vṛ: Śiva's power).
With no other proven (cānyāprasiddhitaḥ — ca+anyā+prasiddhitaḥ, Vṛ: no separate cause established, difference-identity vikalpa-felled).
This world-maker lordship (jagannirmātṛteśitā) is made of non-showing (tadakhyātimayam).
Vṛ: Māyā is Śiva's non-separate power, concealment-play; from that cause alone this non-showing-made world shines; world-shines' makerhood is lordship.
inference: Māyā from power alone, lordship from non-showing: no second cause survives.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is proclaimed through linking?
premises: One alone (ekaiva) through linking (anusaṃdhānāt), she (sā) is proclaimed (proktā).
Of all awarenesses (sarvasaṃvidām): the mother-principle (mātṛtattvam), self-feeling's synonym (svasaṃvedanaparyāya), beginningless (anādi).
Vṛ: the sovereign higher power — linking severed blue-etc. awarenesses across before-after ends — one alone, grounding them, bounding them: the mother's beginningless principle.
inference: Proclamation: one linking mother-principle of all awarenesses, self-feeling itself, beginningless.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What fits the inert?
premises: Whatever grounding (niṣṭhā) of thing-ordering (bhāvavyavasthā) — pervasion (vyāpitvam) and linking (anusaṃdhānam) of the I-sharing him (tasyāhaṃbhāvabhāginaḥ).
That (taj) fits (yujyate) nothing inert (jaḍasya na).
Vṛ: where all things stand settled — awareness-self of full-I-grasp pith, freedom-never-parted — pervasion-as-linking holds everywhere; the unfree inert, grasp-pith-less, cannot host it.
inference: Pervasion and linking belong to I-sharers only: the inert cannot host them.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is the verdict?
premises: So (tatas) within difference (bhede), shining's shining (bhāsasya bhāsamānatā) holds good (ghaṭate).
Hence (tena) said (uktam) in recognition (pratyabhijñāyām): this world (jagat) is that-nondual-made (tadadvayamayaṃ).

Vṛ: holding to non-inertness — in this difference-flashing world, blue-pleasure-etc. shining keeps unspent inward seat while outshining through knowing-power (hence shining-shining holds); holding to non-difference, the inert re-shines — else unshining. So in the glorious Īśvarapratyabhijñā the world is said awareness-nondual-natured. Peace (iti śivam).
inference: Verdict: difference keeps shining-shining; recognition says the world that-nondual-made.
